feedback: Reed's confession follows the strongest interpretive thread I identified: the crossed-out original-contents sentence, continued denial, and admitted glass-side visit. It adds the actual taking and pouring of poison, but those are the confessed acts rather than a new evidentiary mechanism. The line about controlling the version everybody read fits Reed's academic anxiety and gives the crime an emotionally coherent shape. Elle and Monet's admissions are satisfying because their lies become real debts and consequences, rather than vanishing as harmless red herrings. I still regard the solution as earned in character and plausible in method more than uniquely compelled by proof; the finale confirms my choice without independently removing the other physical opportunities.
